ethinyl estradiol.t: May increase plasma levels of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol; consider this effect when selecting an oral contraceptive ( 7.3 ).
Co-administration of atorvastatin calcium and an oral contraceptive increased plasma concentrations of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ].

norethindrone.t: May increase plasma levels of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol; consider this effect when selecting an oral contraceptive ( 7.3 ).
Co-administration of atorvastatin calcium and an oral contraceptive increased plasma concentrations of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ].

digoxin.t: May increase digoxin plasma levels; monitor patients appropriately ( 7.3 ).
When multiple doses of atorvastatin calcium and digoxin were co-administered, steady state plasma digoxin concentrations increased [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ].

gemfibrozil.t: Concomitant use of cyclosporine or gemfibrozil with atorvastatin calcium is not recommended.
Concomitant use of cyclosporine, gemfibrozil, tipranavir plus ritonavir, or glecaprevir plus pibrentasvir with atorvastatin calcium is not recommended.

ritonavir.t: Concomitant use of tipranavir plus ritonavir or glecaprevir plus pibrentasvir with atorvastatin calcium is not recommended.
Concomitant use of cyclosporine, gemfibrozil, tipranavir plus ritonavir, or glecaprevir plus pibrentasvir with atorvastatin calcium is not recommended.

lopinavir.t: In patients taking lopinavir plus ritonavir, or simeprevir, consider the risk/benefit of concomitant use with atorvastatin.

Tipranavir plus ritonavir, glecaprevir plus pibrentasvir, lopinavir plus ritonavir, simeprevir, saquinavir plus ritonavir, darunavir plus ritonavir, fosamprenavir, fosamprenavir plus ritonavir, elbasvir plus grazoprevir, letermovir, nelfinavir, and ledipasvir plus sofosbuvir.

clarithromycin.t: In patients taking clarithromycin or itraconazole, do not exceed atorvastatin calcium 20 mg [see Dosage and Administration (2.5) ].
Erythromycin, clarithromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, posaconazole, and voriconazole.

itraconazole.t: In patients taking clarithromycin or itraconazole, do not exceed atorvastatin calcium 20 mg [see Dosage and Administration (2.5) ].
Erythromycin, clarithromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, posaconazole, and voriconazole.

erythromycin.t: Erythromycin, clarithromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, posaconazole, and voriconazole.

ketoconazole.t: Erythromycin, clarithromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, posaconazole, and voriconazole.

colchicine.t: Cases of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis have been reported with concomitant use of colchicine with atorvastatin calcium.
Consider the risk/benefit of concomitant use of colchicine with atorvastatin calcium.

rifampin.t: Drug Interactions that may Decrease Exposure to Atorvastatin Calcium Tablets Rifampin Clinical Impact:
Concomitant administration of atorvastatin calcium with rifampin, an inducer of cytochrome P450 3A4 and inhibitor of OATP1B1, can lead to variable reductions in plasma concentrations of atorvastatin.

glucose.t: 5.4 Increases in HbA1c and Fasting Serum Glucose Levels Increases in HbA1c and fasting serum glucose levels have been reported with statins, including atorvastatin calcium.

statin.t: Hypersensitivity to atorvastatin or any excipients in atorvastatin calcium tablets.
Hypersensitivity to atorvastatin or any excipient in atorvastatin calcium tablets ( 4 ).
